verdicts.rewritten_summary: New Zimbabwe, 9 July 2018: the health ministry released a 68-page training handbook for all health practitioners on serving gays, sex workers and transgender/non-gender-conforming people in public health institutions. The manual states care for these groups is legal and every provider's duty ('nowhere in policy or law states it is illegal to provide healthcare services to members of key population groups'), issued because patients had avoided clinics fearing mistreatment or police tip-offs by staff. For a trans visitor: formal policy guarantees health-service access including transition-relevant care at public facilities, though day-to-day treatment depends on staff trained under a 2018 handbook.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: GALZ (Gays and Lesbians of Zimbabwe) official site: voluntary membership organisation established 1990, now 4,000+ community members, 35 years of advocacy, 10 affinity groups, 4 resource centres. Services include legal support (explicitly including for 'sodomy' arrests), counselling, hospital-fee assistance and empowerment programmes for LGBTI Zimbabweans. verdicts.rewritten_summary: The 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill amends the 2019 law: it removes the right to self-identification, limits legal recognition to historically accepted categories and intersex individuals, and mandates medical certification for identity recognition - HRW calls it a major reversal of the 2014 rights and urges the president not to sign it (articles dated 26 Mar 2026).
verdicts.note: national framework; record text claims 2026 amendment (rule 5)

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Amendment bill approved by both houses (article 2026, awaiting presidential assent): removes the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court 'third gender' ruling; narrows the 2019 definition of transgender person; government says the narrower definition improves welfare delivery, critics warn it excludes trans men, trans women, non-binary and gender-fluid people; mandatory medical certification described as an attack on privacy and dignity.
verdicts.note: national framework; record text claims 2026 amendment (rule 5)
